Marker and sound track have an owner id (static), because GameFlow adds the scene of the next stage before the old one has left the tree.

contract_issues: §4.9.3 says make uses --shot-fast and 'builds a worktree'. The tag v0.7.0 does not know --shot-fast (this package introduces it), so make renders every frame: 725 s measured against 153-176 s for check. Solution: the flag is passed in both cases (the tag ignores it); that fast and full rendering give the same pictures is shown by the 20 of 20 identical hashes. The tag is exported with git archive, not as a worktree.

§4.2 says --graphics= 'wins over everything', §4.4.2 step 1 says mode = setup.get('gfx', Settings.effective_graphics().mode), so setup.gfx beats the command line. Implemented §4.4.2 literally (tests and the Leistungstest need a fixed mode). Consequence for UI1: attract demos must take setup.gfx from Settings.effective_graphics(), otherwise the rescue switch --graphics=arcade does not reach the demos.

§6 ('prepare() done on the next frame') and §4.4.1/D34 (self-test inside prepare(), spans frames) cannot both hold with a real renderer. Solution: self-test once per run in prepare(), next frame headless and afterwards (see deviations).

§4.4.2 step 5 names only one way the marker goes (2 s of rendered frames). Taken literally, every stage left within 2 s (back to the menu, restart, a demo ended by a key) leaves the marker and forces Arcade at the next start. Solution: orderly exit and fallback remove it too; proven in check_seam abgang and over real process starts.

§4.9.5/§4.9.3: release export templates refuse a scene path on the command line (Godot: binary 'compiled without support for path overrides'), so an exported build cannot run res://scenes/race/race.tscn like the goldens do. Smoke runs of exports must start through '-- --stage=…' (GameFlow). Those frames are not the golden frames: at S1 2,697 pixels differ (backdrop, rows 116-368; measured, the delivered v0.7.0 build behaves the same). Solution: export frames are compared with export frames (new .exe against v0.7.0 .exe, Wine against the Linux export: identical); a golden list for exports would need its own hashes.

scripts/ui/** has no owner in wave 0 (§5), but §4.4.2 wants progress in the loading overlay, §4.4.6 the gfx field in leaderboard entries, §4.7.1 GameFlow calling AudioManager.set_profile(Settings.sound()), D32 the chooser. Solution: the session uses LoadingOverlay as it is and calls set_progress(p) only if the widget has it; everything else is left for UI1 (see notes).

§4.4.1 and Rule 8 require --graphics=arcade for check_glow_occlusion, shoot_vehicles, bench_render, check_sprite_flip and every tool run, but these files and tools/screenshot.sh belong to no wave-0 package. Solution: not edited; tools/run_render_checks.sh passes --graphics=arcade for the two render checks; with no stored choice (and the isolated XDG_DATA_HOME) all of them are Arcade anyway (D32). tools/screenshot.sh, tests/race/shoot_vehicles.gd and bench_render.gd still need an owner.

§4.2 lists flags nobody owns in wave 0: --bench, --bench-out, --no-chooser, --no-prewarm, --no-watchdog, --audio-sync and the debug views other than 'fail'. KERN implemented --graphics, --gfx-preset, --gfx, --gfx-sync (handed to prepare() as ctx.sync), --gfx-debug=fail, --sound and --shot-fast; the others are ignored until their packages read them.

§4.4.2 step 2 ('equal shot times show equal simulation states in both modes') holds for scenes started the normal way (race.tscn standalone, GameFlow): 151 simulation steps at the 2.5 s shot in both modes. A scene added from a process_frame callback is one step behind in Arcade (its first frame has no physics step); that is engine ordering and only matters for test harnesses - check_seam_render.gd therefore launches at physics_frame.

§4.9.2's command line names no quality preset. Under Xvfb the adapter is llvmpipe -> tier 'software' -> recommended preset 'low' (3D scale 75 %), headless the adapter name is empty -> tier 'ok' -> 'medium'. Render checks and Modern goldens that depend on quality must name their preset (--gfx-preset=…); the command line was left as specified.

UI1: Settings API and signals are in ARCHITECTURE.md §15.1. Title question after a crash: Settings.crash_guard and Settings.disarm_crash_guard(); with a marker but no stored choice effective_graphics() also says reason 'crash_guard'. LoadingOverlay.set_progress(p) is picked up by the session as soon as the widget has it. GameFlow has to call AudioManager.set_profile(Settings.sound()) at boot and on sound_profile_changed (which emits the resolved profile).

AU-A: the session calls AudioManager.set_track(track, plan) in _build() and set_track(null, null) when the scene leaves the tree (only if it still owns the track); set_vehicle_state(state) every frame of a running stage (from the countdown on, not during Modern's preparation, not while paused) - whether the receiver has it is checked once when the stage is built; event(name, args) right after the matching AudioManager.play() call. stage_start {countdown_s} comes once before the first simulation step; collision carries {speed_kmh, rel_kmh, heavy, side}, refuel_done {liters, aborted}. A recorder can be injected through RaceSession.audio_hooks (see tests/race3d/check_seam.gd).

contract_issues: 4.6.7 ModelDB.reload(manifest_path) cannot work. On a class name GDScript resolves reload() to Script.reload(keep_state: bool) of the script resource. Evidence: 'SCRIPT ERROR: Invalid type in function 'reload' in base 'GDScript'. Cannot convert argument 1 from String to bool.'; without an argument it silently reloads the script and returns an error code. Solution: ModelDB.load_manifest(manifest_path := "") -> bool.

4.6.4 'COLOR.rgb albedo as sRGB bytes (the shader converts to linear)' is wrong for GL Compatibility. The engine linearises ALBEDO and EMISSION after fragment(); vertex colours and colour uniforms arrive raw. Evidence: unshaded ALBEDO 0.5 displays 128, 0.2 displays 50. Solution: shaders do not convert; energies are applied as pow(e, 1/2.2).

4.5.6 ensure_globals 'adds every missing ce_* global' cannot ask which exist: RenderingServer.global_shader_parameter_get_list() raises 'This function should never be used outside the editor'. Solution: a static flag in ModernMaterials; nothing else may add ce_* globals.

4.5.6 'ce_sun_color / ce_ambient = colour x energy' is underspecified. With sRGB-encoded values and a linear sum the tree impostor was about 4x too bright by moonlight (display 21 against 5). Solution: linear values via ModernMaterials.light_value(), and billboard.gdshader repeats the renderer's arithmetic.

D5/D6 have a consequence the contract does not state (measured). Every pass ends with max(1.055 x^(1/2.4) - 0.055, 0), so a pass below linear 0.0008 contributes nothing; with the post path pinned on, the picture passes through both approximations once more (ALBEDO 0.06 displays 11 without post and 5 with it; 0.04 displays 4 and 0). The sun is added in sRGB space even with the post path on (ground: 27 + 55 displays 87, a linear sum would give 60). Night ambient and moon energies must stay above that floor.

4.6.8 the 2 % tolerance for object/extent_m needs an absolute floor because sprite extents are pixel-quantised. Evidence: streetlight right extent 0.17 in the sprite against 0.16 in the model is 6 % but 1 cm, with a sprite pixel of 3.6 cm. Solution: the validator allows max(2 %, half a sprite pixel + 5 mm).
4.6.3 'No tangents' cannot be checked: compressed surfaces always report a tangent array (packed with the normals, no extra bytes). The validator does not judge it.

4.6.8 the geometry fixture cannot be exact for one set. bmesh.ops.create_uvsphere returns faces in a different order in every process, with the v0.7.0 generators as well (landmarks/fernsehturm_berlin). Solution: order-independent fields ctopo and nstat; a set counts as identical when only topo differs.

4.6.9 the note 'decal patches only in LOD0, >= 1.5 mm above the body' conflicts with the triangle budgets and with z-fighting at distance. Solution: decals cut into the body as one layer for traffic cars.
4.6.5 UV reuse of the road-facing wall on the far wall is not implemented; it would need mirrored charts in the baker. Solution: the `allround` generator parameter.
Section 5 lists billboard.gdshader under PIPE for wave 0, the PIPE 'Files' line in section 6 does not. PIPE delivered it because the impostor needs it; R2 takes it over.
4.6.1 'two bakes byte-identical' holds per output path only: a .res stores a UID derived from its path.

The cache folder tools/blender/_cache3d has no .gitignore entry (the file belongs to KERN). Solution: the folder ignores itself with its own .gitignore and .gdignore; without .gdignore Godot imported every model.glb as a scene.

D3 and section 4.5.2 say the path is integrated 1,900 m ahead. contract_issues: 1. §4.7.1 against §5: GameFlow is to call set_profile(Settings.sound()) at boot, but scripts/ui has no owner before wave 2, so in waves 0 and 1 nothing would ever switch to Modern. Evidence: in the trial merge with KERN no code outside scripts/audio calls set_profile. Solution: the AudioManager reads --sound= and audio.profile at start (same precedence as KERN's Gfx.resolve_sound); the stored setting arrives with UI1.

2. D29 says ducking is scripted bus volume. Measured (Godot 4.7.2, 100 Hz sine, −6 dB): a bus volume change is applied at a mix-block boundary without a ramp – a step of 15 to 33 times the signal's own slope, a click; AudioEffectAmplify ramps across the block (1.0 to 1.5 times). Solution: the scripted gain goes through an Amplify effect on the bus; still scripted, still no sidechain compressor.

3. D29 leaves open what steers the ducking. The engine only offers peak meters per bus, and neither peak nor RMS follows the loudness of an engine. Measured on the car bus with the stand-in engine at idle / 130 km/h / full throttle (−20.4 / −22.7 / −16.2 LUFS): peak −6.4 / −11.1 / −0.3 dBFS, RMS −15.3 / −20.7 / −14.4 dBFS – a peak key would duck the music more at idle than at 130 km/h. Solution: key = loudness of the plan for the driving state (ModernMix.car_lufs), the same in every run.

4. The study's 'static mid dip in the music bus while racing' cannot be built with Godot's band equalisers: they sum band-passes and are not neutral. Measured from impulse responses with every band at 0 dB: EQ10 +1.4 to +3.3 dB (ripple from band to band), EQ21 about +3.9 dB, EQ6 +0.5 to +2.6 dB; the first version with an EQ10 put the race music 2 dB above the plan and gave +1.3 dB at 500 Hz where −3 dB were wanted. Solution: two shelving filters (exact: 0 dB outside the shelf; their gain property is squared, measured 0.841 → −3.01 dB). Picture: renn_eq_frequenzgang.png.

5. §4.7.3 lists MEnv last. A bus can only send to a bus with a lower index – otherwise the engine silently sends to Master. Solution: creation in the order of ModernBuses.GRAPH, ModernBuses.verify() and a test guard it. Worth a sentence in the contract so nobody reads the list as an order.

6. Rule 1 against a defect: the frozen EngineAudio.detach() stops and frees the player of an AudioStreamGenerator in one go. Godot's generator playback keeps a plain pointer to its stream; the audio thread still mixes a fade-out block and then reads the sample rate from freed memory (debugger: −2.1e37, endless loop in the resampler, main thread blocked on the audio lock). With profile switches and a running engine this hung 4 of 29 runs; the Modern code now keeps such streams for 2 s (ModernAudioContext.keep_alive): 0 of 66 runs. In Arcade it could not be triggered in 1500 simulated stage changes. Not fixed because the file is frozen; the lead decides. Proposed fix: keep the stream about 2 s after detach().

7. Attract mode and its check belong to scripts/ui and tests/race (not mine) and know only Arcade: the mode mutes the Arcade buses, tests/race/check_attract.gd samples the Arcade music player (_music, _music_wanted). My side: MSfx follows the mute state of the Arcade bus SFX. The check cannot pass with the Modern profile as written – for UI2 or AU-E.
8. §4.7.1 writes event(name: String, ...): in the autoload (a Node) the parameter would shadow Node.name. Solution: event_name; every call works unchanged.

9. The acceptance item 'headless race' proves less than it sounds: headless nothing is played (as in Arcade), so it covers the state path only. I added a headless run with playback forced (ModernAudio.force_live, the Dummy driver really mixes) and a run under Xvfb. Related: when frame time × Engine.time_scale exceeds 0.35 s of game time, the session counts as gone between two frames in both profiles (the safe-shutdown rule of the AudioManager); sound checks therefore run at time scale 8. QA2's network-wide Modern runs at a high time scale will not exercise the sound.

10. D29 asks for idle about 8 dB below full throttle; the Arcade bank's idle is only 4.1 dB below (measured −17.2 against −13.1 LUFS). No bus level can fix a ratio inside one stream – noted so that nobody tunes audio.modern.levels to chase the idle and cruise targets before AU-B's engine exists.

11. QC 'click detector' (study): implemented as a loop-seam check relative to its surroundings. A click in the middle of a file is not found, and a click just before the seam hides a bad seam (reproduced in the counter-test). A general click detector cannot tell a click from a drum hit; the limit is written into docs/audio-modern.md.

Evidence: 300 GPU particles of 4 s lifetime show 1,307 instead of 20,191 lit pixels after 114 skipped frames - what the RenderingServer advances while drawing stands still while the render loop is off. Chosen: new argument --shot-fast-lead=<s> (default 0.1 s) and the render loop stays on while a Modern stage is prepared. The contract should list the argument and say that the Modern change detectors (§4.9.3) render without --shot-fast or with a lead of at least the longest GPU effect.

§4.4.2 step 2 ('equal shot times show equal simulation states') held only for the race scene started on its own. Started through GameFlow at boot (-- --stage=, the only start of an exported build) the scene is drawn once before its first physics callback, so Arcade is one step behind at every shot time (HUD 0:00.98 against 0:01.00). Chosen: the session measures that lead and credits it to the clocks that stood when a Modern stage goes live; a static counter Screenshotter.preparing also holds a Screenshotter the session does not own (attract demo: 267 steps and the same position in both modes at shot time 6 s). The contract text should name both.

§4.5 (line 593) and the GEO acceptance say 'at most 16 chunks'. modern_path_check.gd --full: the loading rule wants up to 18; with the cap of 16 a piece of road inside the visibility is left out at 209 of 31,488 camera positions, the nearest 456 m away. Chosen: the key graphics.modern.max_chunks now stands in config/game_config.json at 16 (behaviour unchanged). The contract should say 18 or accept the holes - lead decision with the draw budget.

§4.6.1: 'cache key = hash of builder code + parameters + exporter version' was implementable in a way that ignores the sprite catalog (a changed paint left every model 'aus dem Cache'). Chosen: the key also hashes the resolved sprite-catalog entries of the source set and of every served set and the colour tables. The contract should define 'parameters' that way and list --check-keys and _cache3d/export_report.json (timings no longer inside model_meta.json).

§4.6.4: (a) 'for the lamp channels 0-13 COLOR.rgb is the lit colour; unlit the lamp is drawn at 25 %' made the rear number plate beige-grey by day. Chosen: channel 8 is a lit surface like 14 - it keeps albedo and roughness and adds albedo x weight x tail level x plate_energy (day #eeeeea, night #a6a6a3). (b) '25 %' is half the display value = 22 % of the light in the shader (lamp_off 0.5). (c) the contract gives no lamp energies; with the old 3.0 a tail light clipped. Chosen: lamp_energy 1.0 with group gains (brake 2.2, indicators 1.6, head/DRL/reverse 2.0, beacons 2.0) and an overdrive that keeps the hue.

§4.6.6 / §4.6.8: lights[] entries now carry 'dir' (unit vector, where the lamp looks) and 'pos' lies on the lamp instead of in the area centroid (before: up to 28 mm inside the car body, 69 mm at the street light). §4.6.8 should list the new validator rules: minimum projected area per lamp role, car end and level; a coarser level not larger than 2 x + 5 cm2; automatic levels keep >= 80 % of each lamp; anchors at most 3 mm below; at most 8 triangles wound against their normals; no auto_lod on meshes with lamp channels.

§4.6.7: ModelDB.reload() cannot exist - called from outside it resolves to GDScript.reload(keep_state: bool) of the class object ('Invalid type in function reload in base GDScript. Cannot convert argument 1 from String to bool', probe). It is load_manifest(). The section should also list what the renderer packages need: ModelDB.missing(set_ids, lods), request(set_ids, lods, owner), release_all(owner), lod_for_distance() answering 'impostor' beyond the last mesh level, ModernMaterials.shared() / drop_shared() (one instance per process, the class materials sit on the shared meshes), and that ModelFactory.build() / multimesh_parts() return null / [] when any mesh of the level is missing.

§4.11: (a) 'leaving Modern calls ModelDB.release_all()' frees no texture memory - the materials hold the textures (QA: 13.60 MB stay until ModernMaterials.clear()); name both calls. (b) The engine keeps the 3D render buffers after the first Modern stage, also in later Arcade stages (re-measured: 314.4 against 321.8 MB at 1280 x 720) - 'each mode loads only its own assets' cannot hold literally. (c) 'Arcade today 247-259 MB' does not hold here: an Arcade stage holds 314 MB, of which 135.5 MiB are HUD font atlases (82 atlases, already in v0.7.0). Lead decision before R1 and PERF measure against the 260 MB budget.

§4.9.1 target <= 9 min: 517-525 s with wave 0 alone; every later package adds checks. Raise the target or let QA1 run independent headless checks two at a time. Also new: run_tests.sh needs python3 for the model validator.

§4.9.1 / §4.9.2: the generic hook must not trust the exit code alone (a check with a script error printed 'CHECKS OK'), and a render check file must fail on a shader that does not compile (such a material draws nothing). Both are implemented; the contract should state them as rules of the two runners.

D8 / F6: far street lamps cannot rely on emissive geometry alone - the 0.61 m luminaire is shorter than one pixel from about 430 m (inferred from the 711 px focal length, not measured), while Arcade shows its light layer up to the visibility limit. The renderer needs a far-field glow at the 'lights' anchors of props, as the flares for vehicles.

Rule on game runs ('set XDG_DATA_HOME to a folder under your scratch dir'): it must say an absolute path. Godot ignores a relative value with a warning and uses ~/.local/share - this happened to a QA lens and to me. The repository tools now accept only absolute values.
notes_for_next: Renderer packages (R1 ...): ask for models with ModelDB.request(sets, lods, self) and sign off with ModelDB.release_all(self); after loading ask ModelDB.missing() and fall back with reason 'manifest'; use ModernMaterials.shared(); leaving Modern = ModelDB.release_all() plus ModernMaterials.drop_shared(). ModelFactory.build() returns null when a file is missing - show the stand-in. lod_for_distance() can answer ModelDB.IMPOSTOR.

Lights: the vpbr lamp uniforms (lamp_energy, lamp_gain, plate_energy, lights_energy) are set for a picture without a glow pass and can be tuned per class; lights[].pos lies on the lamp and 'dir' looks outward - place flares a little along 'dir'. The player car's lamps sit behind lenses that take about half of their light. Far street lamps need a glow at their anchors (inferred).

R1 decisions and facts: graphics.modern.max_chunks 16 or 18; the curve camera can be given more look but not less (first F1 case at 280 m against the limit of 270 m); the 3D buffers that stay (+7.4 MB at 1280 x 720) belong into the texture budget and the leak baseline; Gfx.watchdog_verdict judges against the display's frame time, so on a 120/144 Hz display a steady 60 fps would count as slow (inferred from the code, not measured).

QA1: render tests/golden/modern_*.md5 without --shot-fast or with --shot-fast-lead; add the second identity list (menus, start through GameFlow, pause, 1280 x 800); give tools/screenshot.sh the absolute-XDG block and --graphics=arcade; the Modern smoke frames of the exports are now e1050b15... / bfd979fa... / 0bed7652... (stub renderer, Linux and Wine alike); under Wine 9.0 keep TMPDIR unset or short.

AS1: cut decals along their contour, use the same lamp outlines for all levels and add a bounds check; every traffic design needs its own indicator fields (validator: cars >= 60 cm2 from behind and >= 40 from ahead per side, player car >= 60 / 15); player car lenses, grille, rims, interior; showroom stays false until an A/B picture passes. A change in the sprite catalog now re-exports exactly the models that read it.

AS4 / AS5a: the first baked_cutout model is the first end-to-end run of the cut-out path (the render check only has a synthetic cut-out quad). No auto_lod on meshes with lamp channels - the validator refuses it.

UI1 / UI2: call AudioManager.set_profile(Settings.sound()) at boot and on change (no caller exists yet); start the attract demo's timer when the stage goes live - today the preparation of a Modern stage counts into the 30 s (6 frames with the stub renderer, progress bar 192 against 188 px at the same shot time); the loading overlay swallows keys during the preparation (QA, inferred); the HUD font draws 135.5 MiB of atlases per stage.

AU-B / AU-C / AU-D: never name a class of scripts/audio/modern, scripts/race3d or ModelDB as a type, preload or constant in a file an Arcade start loads - check_arcade_lean.gd fails then. Idle -20.4 LUFS (plan -24) and cruise -22.7 LUFS (plan -21) come from the stand-in engine. audio_qc.py now fails on a sound file without a manifest entry (--allow-unknown for work in progress).

Lead: open decisions - max_chunks 16/18, frozen EngineAudio.detach(), texture budget against the font atlases, run-time target of run_tests.sh, margin of the curve camera at gate 1, --shot-fast rule for the Modern goldens.
Everyone: Godot ignores a relative XDG_DATA_HOME and falls back to the real user folder; the repository tools guard against it now, own helper scripts must do the same.
